context.process_name: AEA Due to Managers Workbook Procedure
context.objective: Document how we carry out AEA Due to Managers Workbook Procedure, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: AEA's due-to-manager workbook is quarterly. We start only when both AEA's email confirms the quarter is closed and AEA-generated Bilixio reports are saved to the shared drive. GPFS cannot access Bilixio directly. The preparer builds a quarterly workbook per fund, reconciles every project code and total to Sage with zero differences, saves an invoice PDF and updates the annual workbook. We email AEA when reports are ready. Whether AEA acceptance must be retained before closing is unconfirmed.
How does the preparer reconcile the project codes and totals in the workbook to Sage?

Use the Sage GL balance and the approved project-code mapping. Subtract a GP-project amount only where a prior approved workbook, expense matrix or client-approved source supports it. Do not infer the exclusion from its label. If its amount or approval is unclear, stop and get AEA or GPFS reviewer direction. Resolve differences to exactly zero for each code and in total, paste the Sage screenshot, sign and date the reconciliation, and repeat it for the full-year workbook.
When the workbook is ready, what does AEA do next, and what—if anything—must happen before you consider the work closed?

GPFS checks off all handled funds in the expense matrix and verifies that each has its quarterly workbook, complete readable PDF, annual update and signed zero-difference support. Then GPFS emails AEA and retains the email and package location. AEA reviews and distributes internally. As I mentioned, whether GPFS has to retain AEA acceptance before closing is unresolved. No individual approver is named.
What business result does the due-to-manager workbook process provide to AEA or GPFS?

AEA receives the supported invoice amounts for every GPFS-handled LP fund in a quarterly workbook and PDF. It can review the package and distribute the invoices internally. The zero-difference Sage reconciliation and annual workbook establish that the numbers agree. Preparing off-cycle packages and distributing the invoices are outside GPFS's work.
Does the work differ across the GPFS-handled LP funds, or is the same process used for each?

All in-scope AEA funds use the quarterly process and the per-code and total zero checks. The report population, project codes and workbook structure depend on the fund in the expense matrix. Whether the GP-project adjustment applies needs approved evidence for the particular case. The full project-code master and approved templates by fund remain open. One prior Q1 started in early April, but that is not a contractual deadline.
What does the reviewer check in the signed zero-difference reconciliation before GPFS emails AEA?
